title: Boeing vs. Lockheed Martin: Which Essential U.S. Aerospace Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
author: Brendan Coffey
description: The article compares Boeing and Lockheed Martin as aerospace investment options for 2026. Boeing is undergoing a turnaround with strong commercial aviation demand and record backlogs, but faces operational challenges, high debt (10.0x debt-to-equity), and negative free cash flow. Lockheed Martin offers stability with steady profitability, lower leverage (3.2x debt-to-equity), strong free cash flow ($6.9B), and long-term F-35 program revenue visibility. The author recommends Lockheed Martin as the better value investment due to its cheaper valuation multiples (17.3x forward P/E vs. Boeing's 49.7x) and fortress-like business model.

Lockheed Martin is recommended as the better buy due to stable profitability (7% net margin), lower leverage (3.2x debt-to-equity), strong free cash flow ($6.9B), attractive valuation (17.3x forward P/E), and long-term revenue visibility from the F-35 program extending into the 2040s. The company offers fortress-like stability and reliable government contract revenue.

title: Great News for RTX Investors (Hint: It Relates to Its Record $289 Billion Backlog)
author: Lee Samaha
description: RTX's $289 billion backlog is expected to grow significantly, potentially reaching $460.5 billion by 2028. CEO Chris Calio highlighted strong demand across commercial aerospace and defense markets, including a $22.9 billion Tomahawk cruise missile order and five framework agreements with the Department of Defense that could increase volumes 2-4x. With 45% of RPO tied to long-term maintenance contracts and lower execution risk compared to competitors, RTX is well-positioned for sustained revenue growth.

title: Should You Invest in the iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA)?
author: Zacks.Com
description: The iShares U.S. Aerospace & Defense ETF (ITA) is recommended as a solid option for investors seeking broad exposure to the aerospace and defense sector. With $12.68 billion in assets, a low 0.37% expense ratio, and a Zacks ETF Rank of 2 (Buy), ITA tracks the Dow Jones U.S. Select Aerospace & Defense Index. The ETF has returned 6.54% over the past year with moderate risk (beta of 0.74), though it is heavily concentrated in its top 10 holdings which account for 77.23% of assets.

title: Boeing's New MQ-25A Stingray Drone Costs $184 Million ... or Less
author: Rich Smith
description: Boeing has been awarded a $552 million contract to deliver three MQ-25A Stingray refueling drones to the U.S. Navy, with the contract implying a cost of $184 million per drone—over 10% below initial estimates of $207-209 million. While delivery is several years behind schedule (expected 2029), the potential for under-budget delivery could enhance Boeing's reputation and lead to additional contracts.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Boeing secured a $552 million Navy contract with unit costs 10% below initial estimates, demonstrating potential for profitable production and cost efficiency. Delivering under budget could enhance the company's reputation and lead to additional defense contracts, offsetting delays in the program timeline.

title: Cathie Wood Sold Palantir and AMD, Then Poured $3.35 Million Into Archer Aviation. Is ARK Betting Big on Flying Taxis?
author: Keith Noonan
description: Cathie Wood's Ark Innovation ETF sold shares of Palantir and AMD while investing $3.35 million in Archer Aviation, signaling growing confidence in the eVTOL aircraft maker. The moves appear to be profit-taking on the larger positions while increasing exposure to the high-risk, high-reward aviation technology sector, particularly following Archer's Boeing partnership deal.

insights.sentiment_reasoning: Ark increased its investment position in Archer despite the stock being down 31% YTD and 62% from highs, indicating confidence in the company's long-term potential. The Boeing partnership deal and acquisition of subsidiaries are viewed as positive developments that improve Archer's positioning in eVTOL technology.

Ark sold shares as a profit-taking move following significant gains, not due to loss of confidence in the company. Palantir remains the 11th-largest holding in the fund, indicating continued belief in the company's fundamentals.
